bibliography.title: Probabilistic Kernel Function for Fast Angle Testing

page_map.document_layout: Two-column ICLR layout. Main narrative ends p.9; main Figure 2 floats on p.10, which also begins References. Figures 3/4 and Figures 5–9 reduce readable text area with wide multi-panel or diagram floats.
page_map.boundary_note: References occupy physical pp.10–12; Appendix A begins p.13. Main_pages includes p.10 because Figure 2 is a main-text result float; the narrative section 8 ends p.9.

abstract_sentences.text: In this paper, we study the angle testing problem in the context of similarity search in high-dimensional Euclidean spaces and propose two projection-based probabilistic kernel functions, one designed for angle comparison and the other for angle thresholding.

evidence.anchor: propose two projection-based probabilistic kernel functions

abstract_sentences.text: Unlike existing approaches that rely on random projection vectors drawn from Gaussian distributions, our approach leverages reference angles and adopts a deterministic structure for the projection vectors.

evidence.anchor: leverages reference angles and deterministic structure

abstract_sentences.text: Notably, our kernel functions do not require asymptotic assumptions, such as the number of projection vectors tending to infinity, and can be theoretically and experimentally shown to outperform Gaussian-distribution-based kernel functions.

We apply the proposed kernel function to Approximate Nearest Neighbor Search (ANNS) and demonstrate that our approach achieves a 2.5×–3× higher query-per-second (QPS) throughput compared to the widely-used graph-based search algorithm HNSW.
Our code and data are available at https://github.com/KejingLu-810/KS.

claim_closure.claim: Reference angle plus random rotation replaces the Gaussian asymptotic relationship.
claim_closure.method_response: Eq.2–3 use Z_S and A_S with H; Remarks explain the generalization.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Lemma 4.2/4.3 give conditional exact relationships, but require d≥3 and ψ<π/2; experiments do not measure all angles.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion restates reference-angle kernels without extending the conditions.

claim_closure.claim: Smaller reference angle improves kernel accuracy.
claim_closure.method_response: J(S), Ssym/Spol and multi-level L are chosen to reduce reference angle.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Lemma B.1, Figure 5 and KS1 tables align structure/cosine with recall, but no direct controlled error curve is supplied.

evidence.anchor: increasing L significantly raises the cosine

claim_closure.claim: KS1 improves CEOs by up to about 0.8%.
claim_closure.method_response: KS1-prime substitutes Ssym/Spol for Gaussian projections in the shared Alg.5/6 protocol.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Table 1 reports the main ten-run comparison; Tables 4/5 provide top-2/top-10 sensitivity and preserve exceptions.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion states slight improvement over CEOs.

evidence.anchor: Comparison of recall rates (%) for k-MIPS

claim_closure.claim: KS2 gives a probabilistic graph-routing test.
claim_closure.method_response: Eq.9 and Algorithm 7 insert KS2_Test before exact distance; Corollary 6.2 states (δ,0.5)-routing.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Figures 1, 6 and 7 show end-task curves, but do not directly estimate false-prune/true-keep probabilities.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion recovers KS2 as the graph-search application.

claim_closure.claim: HNSW+KS2 is faster and smaller than HNSW/PEOs.
claim_closure.method_response: Eq.9 simplifies per-edge operations and stores two scalars plus L bytes; L controls cost.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Figure 1 supports the curve ordering and p.9 reports indexing overhead; Word and GIST exceptions plus missing raw points limit generality.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion says better search performance than existing ANNS approaches.

claim_closure.claim: Ssym/Spol is better than Gaussian/random projection structure.
claim_closure.method_response: Algorithms 1/2 use antipodal/cross-polytope structure; Appendix Algorithm 3 supplies random baseline.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Lemma B.1 proves an expected lower-bound relation against random projection and tables show most empirical gains, not every cell.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: Conclusion mentions projection-vector structure without claiming universal optimality.

claim_closure.claim: L controls accuracy, space and time.
claim_closure.method_response: Multi-level construction and Lemma 5.1 expose L in projection and per-vector costs.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Figures 2, 5 and 8 show the predicted trends across the tested dimensions/datasets.

final_judgment.single_storyline: Use reference angle as the shared geometric intermediate: replace Gaussian extreme-order asymptotics with an exact random-rotation relationship, optimize projection structure to reduce that angle, then instantiate KS1 comparison and KS2 routing.
final_judgment.main_body_keeps: Problems 1.1/1.2, Eq.2–4, Lemmas 4.2/4.3, Ssym/Spol rationale, Lemma 5.1, Eq.9/Corollary 6.2, Table 1, Figures 1/2 and the main Word/L boundary.
final_judgment.appendix_moves: Proofs, full algorithms, notation, dataset/parameter details, k/top-s0/L/NSSG robustness and Figures 3–9 move to Appendix A–D; conceptual self-sufficiency remains, but reproducibility and uncertainty review require the appendix.
final_judgment.best_pattern: One measurable intermediate quantity A_S/reference angle is threaded through conditional CDF, J(S), projection algorithms, L sensitivity and benchmark interpretation.
final_judgment.largest_gap: Theory is conditional and empirical superiority is mostly curve-level plus a ten-run mean without seeds, dispersion, raw QPS values or a direct reference-angle-to-error test; Word/GIST exceptions bound the broad claims.
final_judgment.transfer_rule: Choose an intermediate quantity that the method can manipulate and theory can identify; predict its change before reporting the final benchmark, then use matched settings to test both the quantity and outcome.
final_judgment.transfer_boundary: The rule applies only when the intermediate quantity and estimand are invariant across methods; changing graph connectivity, query budget or data regime together prevents a causal reading.
